title: EIP-8142: Block-in-Blobs (BiB)
description: Ensures execution payload data availability via blobs
author: Kevaundray Wedderburn (@kevaundray), Ignacio Hagopian (@jsign), Jihoon Song <jihoon.song@ethereum.org>, Francesco Risitano (@frisitano), Thomas Thiery (@soispoke) <thomas.thiery@ethereum.org>, Toni Wahrstätter (@nerolation), Péter Garamvölgyi (@thegaram)
laymanDescription: If validators check blocks with a proof instead of running the transactions themselves, nobody is forced to download what the block contains, and a producer could publish a valid proof while keeping the contents to itself. This proposal requires that data to be published as blobs in the same block, so it is always available.
benefits: Keeps block contents available once validators verify by proof instead of re-execution
Stops a builder withholding data to become the only party able to build the next block
Preserves the data that RPC providers and indexers need, since they must still re-execute
tradeoffs: Payload data consumes blob gas, competing with transaction blobs under the same limits
Access lists must be published even though they could in principle be recomputed
Uses uncompressed data for now; adding compression later would be a breaking change
